general_information.Description: This course provides a foundation for understanding operations management in a global context. It utilizes the frameworks to analyze how organizations direct, design, deliver, and develop their operations across borders. Specifically, the course covers definitions and concepts of operations management, issues of operations performance, operations strategy, structure and scope of supply, process design and technology, people in operations, planning and control, capacity management, inventory management, operations improvement, lean operations, quality management, risk management, and recovery.

description: This course provides a foundation for understanding operations management in a global context. It utilizes the frameworks to analyze how organizations direct, design, deliver, and develop their operations across borders. Specifically, the course covers definitions and concepts of operations management, issues of operations performance, operations strategy, structure and scope of supply, process design and technology, people in operations, planning and control, capacity management, inventory management, operations improvement, lean operations, quality management, risk management, and recovery.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Define and explain the fundamental concepts, terminology, and operational processes in international operations management, including the Input-Transformation-Output model, the process hierarchy, and the 4Vs framework (Volume, Variety, Variation, Visibility).

Analyze the strategic impact of operations decisions on corporate performance across five core performance objectives (Quality, Speed, Dependability, Flexibility, Cost) and evaluate market requirement trade-offs using the Efficient Frontier and Polar Representation.
Evaluate global supply network configurations, offshore/nearshore production strategies, and international facility locations using quantitative tools such as the Weighted-Score Method.

Apply appropriate process designs, manufacturing process types (Project, Batch, Mass, Continuous), and facility layout configurations (Cellular, Product, Functional) to optimize shop-floor material flow and assembly line balancing.

Execute capacity planning, inventory management, and scheduling calculations using operational tools and metrics including Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), ABC Analysis, and Materials Requirements Planning (MRP) logic.

Formulate and propose operations improvement plans by applying Lean manufacturing philosophy (eliminating 7 Wastes/Muda, Value Stream Mapping), Total Quality Management (TQM), risk management, and recovery
Demonstrate the ability to produce a clear, structured academic written report and deliver an effective oral presentation analyzing international manufacturing setup and operational challenges.
Practice effective teamwork, communication, and cross-cultural problem-solving skills to collaboratively design and manage complex global operations projects.
